items.title: We're Living in the Age of the Imperial CEO
items.summary: Anthropic is joining other hot tech companies in going public with a dual-class share structure that keeps its founders in control, following a pattern set by peers.
items.why_it_matters: An Anthropic IPO with entrenched founder control would set governance terms for the next wave of AI listings.

items.title: [AINews] Google admits AI Mode hurts Search revenue; -15% $500B drop worst since 2004 IPO. AI Bear Market coming?
items.summary: Google acknowledged that its AI Mode search feature is cannibalizing traditional search ad revenue, coinciding with a roughly 15%, $500 billion drop in market value, the company's worst stock reaction since its 2004 IPO.
items.why_it_matters: The first clear admission that a lab's own AI product is hurting its core revenue line feeds broader doubts about AI monetization.

items.title: The Tangled Web of AI Bets Is Reason to Fear Tech Stocks
items.summary: Vendor financing arrangements among AI companies, cloud providers and chipmakers have returned in a new form, and this circular web of deals amplifies the AI trade's swings in both directions.
items.why_it_matters: Interlocking vendor-financing deals mean a slowdown in AI spending could hit tech stocks harder and faster than a simple demand dip would.

items.title: Do the math: How we took over ChatGPT accounts
items.summary: Security researchers at Parameter Labs describe an exploit chain against ChatGPT's HTML previews (formerly Canvas) sandboxed-iframe feature, abusing OpenAI's bundled MathLive JavaScript library to break out of the sandbox and take over user accounts.
items.why_it_matters: A working account-takeover chain against ChatGPT's own sandboxing shows how hard it is to keep untrusted code safely contained in AI products.

items.title: Is this the first clear evidence of AI's impact on the labour market?
items.summary: The FT examines data showing productivity rising and employment falling in the tech sector, while the picture is far less clear in other industries, raising the question of whether this is the first measurable sign of AI displacing jobs.
items.why_it_matters: Clear data on AI's labor-market effects would reshape policy and business debates well beyond tech.

items.title: DeepSeek Drops Enhanced Coding Agent With Aim to Rival Anthropic
items.summary: DeepSeek has released a prototype of a more autonomous coding agent, aiming to challenge Anthropic's popular Claude Code. The move signals intensifying competition among AI labs in the agentic coding tools space.
items.why_it_matters: A credible Chinese challenger to Claude Code raises the competitive stakes in the fast-growing agentic coding market.

items.title: OpenAI pares fundraising goal, now seeking up to $20 billion in latest round
items.summary: OpenAI has reduced the target size of its latest funding round to as much as $20 billion, according to a person familiar with the deal. The round is still open and the figures could still change.
items.why_it_matters: A scaled-back ask from the industry's bellwether is a read on investor appetite for AI mega-rounds.

items.title: Kioxia Shares Tumble After Outlook Suggests Demand Leveling Off
items.summary: Kioxia shares fell as much as 15% after the memory maker gave a cautious demand outlook, fueling concerns that AI-driven growth in memory chips may be leveling off.
items.why_it_matters: A major memory supplier flagging slowing demand is an early signal the AI hardware boom could be cooling.

items.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse's Brain
items.summary: A biotech startup let an autonomous AI agent choose a gene therapy and successfully perform an injection into a live mouse's brain, demonstrating AI systems taking on hands-on lab research tasks.
items.why_it_matters: Letting an AI agent make and execute real experimental decisions in a living animal is a striking preview of automated research labs.

items.title: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
items.summary: Cisco Talos documents a new infostealer, nicknamed Volta-Autodoxer, that uses an AI model to automatically prioritize and 'autodox' victims by collecting and valuing stolen data such as credentials, card numbers and Discord sessions.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete example of attackers operationalizing AI models inside malware to make cybercrime more efficient.
